2607.08489.title: VEGAS: Human-Aligned Video Caption Evaluation via Gaze
2607.08489.paper_summary: Vision-language models excel at video captioning, yet typically generate descriptions that fail to capture individual viewers' attention. We propose VEGAS (Video caption Evaluation via GAze Score), a training-free metric that leverages test-time gaze to sample personalized, attention-aligned text. It is a cross-modal, information-theoretic metric that quantifies how well a candidate caption matches a viewer's focus. To evaluate VEGAS, we curate a dataset of egocentric activities and instructional slides paired with synchronized gaze and reference annotations. We then select captions based on VEGAS via rejection sampling without model retraining. Experiments show that VEGAS-selected captions align significantly better with human focus and improve downstream caption-to-video retrieval, demonstrating the practical utility of incorporating viewer attention during inference.
2607.08489.paper_summary_zh: 視覺語言模型在影片標題生成方面表現優異，但通常生成的描述無法吸引個別觀眾的注意。我們提出了VEGAS（透過注視評估影片標題），這是一種無需訓練的指標，利用測試時的注視來抽樣個性化、與注意力對齊的文本。這是一種跨模態的信息理論指標，量化候選標題與觀眾焦點的匹配程度。為了評估VEGAS，我們整理了一個包含自我中心活動和配有同步注視及參考註釋的教學幻燈片的數據集。然後，我們根據VEGAS通過拒絕抽樣選擇標題，而無需重新訓練模型。實驗顯示，VEGAS選擇的標題與人類焦點的對齊程度顯著提高，並改善了下游的標題到影片檢索，顯示在推理過程中納入觀眾注意力的實用性。
